title: How the Maya Tracked Venus Without Telescopes
hook: Maya astronomers calculated Venus orbits to within two hours of modern NASA clocks.

scenes.text: Deep in the Mesoamerican rainforest, ancient Maya priest-astronomers turned temple towers into precision celestial observatories.

scenes.text: Without optical glass lenses or metal instruments, they tracked celestial bodies using simple crossed wooden sighting sticks.

scenes.text: Their primary obsession was Venus: calculated as having a synodic cycle of 583.92 days—matching modern atomic clock measurements within hours.

scenes.text: Venus was viewed as the fierce herald of war; kings scheduled military invasions and coronation rites around its morning rise.

scenes.text: Their calendar interlocked the 260-day sacred count with the 365-day solar year, creating a 52-year cycle where time itself seemed to loop.
